# Password reset

The worked example of the semantic model (§5.1): one outcome, the
requirement that serves it, a constraint on that requirement, and the
decision taken between two options. Each `## <ID> · <type>` opens a record;
a line `<kind> <ID>` inside one is a relation. Warrants, tickets and the
roadmap name these records by id; `war impact REQ-pr1` lists what a change
to one affects. docs/TYPES.md explains the format.

## OUT-pr1 · outcome

A user who forgot their password regains access without support.

## REQ-pr1 · requirement
implements OUT-pr1

A reset token expires 15 minutes after issue.

## CON-pr1 · constraint
constrains REQ-pr1

Tokens are single-use and stored hashed.

## DEC-pr1 · decision
selected_over OPT-pr1, OPT-pr2
constrains REQ-pr1

Signed, stateless tokens with a server-side revocation list: expiry is
checked from the token itself, and a used or revoked token is refused by
the list.

## OPT-pr1 · option

Random opaque tokens stored server-side, looked up on every use.

## OPT-pr2 · option

Signed tokens with no server-side state at all; a used token cannot be
refused before it expires.

# Host Corpus — Software Architecture Specification

Version 0.1.0. This document governs the program `Host Corpus`; every Warrant
in `docs/warrants/` traces to it through `[[implements]]` refs into §106 and
`[[roadmap]]` refs into §98. It is a controlled document: `war sas propose
<version>` records a revision, a human accepts it with `war sign <version>
--ssh-sign`, and Warrants pin the accepted revision (OpenWarrant SAS §101).

Write the architecture here. The three sections below are the ones the tool
reads; keep their headings and shapes, and change everything else.

## 6.10. Levels

| Level | What it is | Who closes it |
|---|---|---|
| Release | this SAS at an accepted version | a human, `war sign <version>` |
| Objective | one §98 phase, reached when its Exit holds | the records of its Warrants |
| Requirement | one §106 row, satisfied by the Warrants that implement it | resolved Warrants |
| Warrant | one bounded intervention, authorized and resolved by a human | `war sign <alias>` |
| Milestone / Stage | a checkpoint inside a Warrant; a dispatchable unit of work | evidence and verification |

A SAS and a Warrant are the same class of document at two levels: one SAS per
program, many Warrants under it. Starting a program means writing this file;
starting a unit of work means `war new`.

## 98. Implementation phases

### Phase 1 — Adopt OpenWarrant

Deliver:

- this SAS at an accepted revision;
- the first Warrant, `HC-WAR-0001`, authorized, delivered, verified and resolved;
- `docs/authority/roles.toml` and `allowed_signers`, written by a human.

Exit:

- one Warrant has gone from `war new` to a human-signed resolution with an independent verification on record.

### Phase 2 — First real work

Deliver:

- the program's own Warrants, one per bounded intervention.

Exit:

- the first §106 requirement beyond adoption is satisfied by a resolved Warrant.

## 106. Architecture requirements index

Stable identifiers for traceability. A Warrant's `[[implements]]` ref names a
row here; `war check` refuses a ref that names no row.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| HC-SAS-RQ-001 | This SAS is accepted by a human signature and every Warrant pins the accepted revision |
| HC-SAS-RQ-002 | Every Warrant is authorized and resolved by a human, never by the performer |
| HC-SAS-RQ-003 | Every resolution rests on an independent verification and recorded gate evidence |
